title: The curse on the land
summary: A curse affects property across the land; people cling to what they own and guard it with swords.

explicit_facts.text: A great curse came upon all the land because of the people's iniquity; tools or swords left in their usual places could not be found the next day.
People held tightly to their possessions, neither borrowing nor lending, and kept sword hilts in their right hands to defend property, lives, wives, and children.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People guarding their property with swords in hand.
unspecified_visual_details: The curse's visible appearance, if any.
The people's clothing, dwellings, and individual identities.

narration.text: there began to be a great curse upon all the land
every man kept the hilt of his sword in his right hand

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the curse as a visible supernatural force or show a specific item disappearing; the text gives no visible manifestation.

title: Coriantumr pursues the brother of Shared
summary: Two years after Shared's death, his brother battles Coriantumr. Coriantumr beats him and pursues him to the wilderness of Akish. The brother of Shared battles Coriantumr there, and many thousands fall by the sword.

explicit_facts.text: After two years and Shared's death, the brother of Shared battled Coriantumr; Coriantumr beat him and pursued him to the wilderness of Akish.
The brother of Shared battled Coriantumr in the wilderness of Akish; the battle was exceedingly sore, and many thousands fell by the sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Combatants fight with swords in the wilderness of Akish.
unspecified_visual_details: The brother of Shared's name and appearance.
The wilderness's terrain and the combatants' clothing.

narration.text: Coriantumr did beat him and did pursue him to the wilderness of Akish.
many thousands fell by the sword.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The pursuit precedes the battle in the wilderness; do not depict them as simultaneous.
prohibited_inventions: Do not reverse who pursues whom.
Do not invent a name for the brother of Shared or depict gore.

title: A night attack and seizure of the throne
summary: After Coriantumr lays siege to the wilderness, the brother of Shared attacks part of Coriantumr's drunken army by night. He comes to Moron and takes Coriantumr's throne.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr laid siege to the wilderness; the brother of Shared marched out by night and slew part of Coriantumr's army while they were drunk.
The brother of Shared came to the land of Moron and placed himself upon Coriantumr's throne.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The night attack takes place in the wilderness under cover of darkness.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the throne and the exact route from the wilderness to Moron.

narration.text: the brother of Shared did march forth out of the wilderness by night
placed himself upon the throne of Coriantumr

prohibited_inventions: Do not combine the night attack and the throne-taking into one simultaneous moment.

title: Strength gained by both armies
summary: Coriantumr dwelt with his army in the wilderness for two years and received great strength for his army. Gilead, the brother of Shared, also received great strength for his army because of secret combinations.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr dwelt with his army in the wilderness for two years and received great strength for his army.
Gilead was the brother of Shared and received great strength for his army because of secret combinations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Coriantumr's army can be depicted with him in the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: Gilead's location and appearance.
How either army gained strength.
The nature of the secret combinations.

narration.text: for the space of two years
whose name was Gilead

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses do not establish that the two armies were together or that their gains occurred at the same moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict secret combinations as an organization with invented rituals or symbols.
Do not place Gilead in the wilderness solely because Coriantumr was there.

title: Gilead is murdered
summary: Gilead's high priest murders him while he sits upon his throne.

explicit_facts.text: Gilead's high priest murdered him as he sat upon his throne.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Gilead is seated on a throne when the murder occurs.
unspecified_visual_details: The high priest's identity and appearance, the weapon, and the throne room.

narration.text: his high priest murdered him as he sat upon his throne

prohibited_inventions: Do not add dialogue, motive, weapon, or graphic injury.

title: Lib takes the kingdom
summary: A member of a secret combination murders Gilead in a secret pass and takes the kingdom. The man's name is Lib, and he is described as taller than anyone else among the people.

explicit_facts.text: One of the secret combinations murdered Gilead in a secret pass and obtained the kingdom; his name was Lib, a man of great stature, more than any other among the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lib is notably taller than people around him.
unspecified_visual_details: Lib's precise height and appearance, and whether Gilead is visible during the murder.

narration.text: his name was Lib
a man of great stature

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific secret-combination symbol, ritual, or motive.

title: Coriantumr battles Lib
summary: In Lib's first year, Coriantumr comes to Moron and battles him. Lib wounds Coriantumr's arm, but Coriantumr's army presses forward and Lib flees to the seashore.

explicit_facts.text: In Lib's first year, Coriantumr came to Moron and battled Lib.
Lib struck Coriantumr's arm, wounding him; Coriantumr's army pressed forward on Lib, who fled to the seashore borders.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Coriantumr's arm is injured, without a need to show blood or graphic detail.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the armies, weapons, and landscape.

narration.text: Lib did smite upon his arm
he fled to the borders upon the seashore

prohibited_inventions: Do not add graphic injury or merge the later seashore battle into this moment.

title: Battle by the sea
summary: Coriantumr pursues Lib, who battles him on the seashore and drives Coriantumr's army back to the wilderness of Akish.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr pursued Lib, and Lib battled him upon the seashore.
Lib struck Coriantumr's army, which fled again to the wilderness of Akish.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The combat takes place on a shoreline.
unspecified_visual_details: The shoreline's specific features and the direction of the army's flight.

narration.text: Lib gave battle unto him upon the seashore
they fled again to the wilderness of Akish

prohibited_inventions: Do not show the flight to the wilderness as simultaneous with the seashore combat.

title: The armies converge at Agosh
summary: Lib pursues Coriantumr to the plains of Agosh, where Coriantumr has taken all the people with him. Coriantumr battles Lib and kills him; Lib's brother then attacks, and Coriantumr flees before his army.

explicit_facts.text: Lib pursued Coriantumr to the plains of Agosh; Coriantumr had taken all the people with him as he fled.
Coriantumr battled Lib and smote him until he died; then Lib's brother attacked in his place, and Coriantumr fled before that army.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people travel with Coriantumr as he flees.
unspecified_visual_details: The brother of Lib's name and appearance, and how the people are organized.

narration.text: he smote upon him until he died

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the brother of Lib's name or show graphic injury.

title: Shiz's campaign
summary: Lib's brother, Shiz, pursues Coriantumr, overthrows many cities, kills women and children, and burns cities. Fear of Shiz spreads throughout the land, with people crying out about his advancing army.

explicit_facts.text: Lib's brother was named Shiz; he pursued Coriantumr, overthrew many cities, slew women and children, and burned cities.
Fear of Shiz spread through the land, where a cry went forth asking who could stand before his army and declaring that it swept the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A city burns as Shiz's forces advance; fear is conveyed through the people's visible reactions.
unspecified_visual_details: The cities' identities, the people who voice the cry, and Shiz's appearance.

narration.text: there went a fear of Shiz throughout all the land
Who can stand before the army of Shiz?

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the metaphor “sweepeth the earth” as a literal supernatural event.
Do not combine the separate acts across multiple cities into one simultaneous event.

title: People gather into armies
summary: People gather into armies across the land and divide, with some joining Shiz and others joining Coriantumr.

explicit_facts.text: People began to flock together in armies throughout the land.

title: The land strewn with the dead
summary: The long war leaves the land covered with bodies. The armies move from battle to battle without burying the dead, leaving men, women, and children across the land.
characters: the armies of Shiz and Coriantumr

explicit_facts.text: The prolonged war and bloodshed left the whole land covered with bodies of the dead.
The war moved so swiftly that no one buried the dead; the armies marched from bloodshed to bloodshed, leaving the bodies of men, women, and children across the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A wide view may show bodies across the landscape without graphic detail.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact landscape, number of bodies, and whether survivors are visible.

narration.text: the whole face of the land was covered with the bodies of the dead
there was none left to bury the dead

prohibited_inventions: Do not show gore, blood, or severed body parts.

title: The people troubled by the stench
summary: The scent of the dead spreads across the land, troubling the people day and night.

explicit_facts.text: The scent spread across the land, and the people were troubled by it by day and by night.

title: Shiz's pursuit and the warning to Coriantumr
summary: Shiz continues pursuing Coriantumr, having sworn to avenge his slain brother; the narration notes the Lord's wrath and the people's wickedness and destruction.

explicit_facts.text: Shiz did not cease pursuing Coriantumr; he had sworn to avenge his brother's blood, and the word of the Lord to Ether was that Coriantumr should not fall by the sword.
The narration says the Lord visited the people in the fulness of his wrath, and their wickedness and abominations had prepared a way for their everlasting destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Shiz and Coriantumr may be shown at a distance to represent the ongoing pursuit.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord's visible appearance, if any; the verses do not describe one.

narration.text: Shiz did not cease to pursue Coriantumr
their wickedness and abominations had prepared a way

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Verse 25 is narratorial teaching, not a described visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly or invent a visual form for divine wrath.

summary: Shiz pursues Coriantumr eastward to the seashore borders, where Coriantumr battles Shiz for three days.

explicit_facts.text: Shiz pursued Coriantumr eastward to the seashore borders, where Coriantumr battled Shiz for three days.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The armies are engaged in battle by the seashore.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact terrain and the sequence of combat across the three days.

title: Shiz's army retreats to Corihor
summary: The destruction among Shiz's armies frightens the people, who flee before Coriantumr's armies to Corihor and force inhabitants who will not join them away. Shiz's people camp in Corihor's valley; Coriantumr camps in Shurr's valley near hill Comnor, gathers his armies there, and sounds a trumpet to invite Shiz's armies to battle.

explicit_facts.text: The destruction among Shiz's armies frightened the people; they fled before Coriantumr's armies to Corihor, sweeping away inhabitants who would not join them.
Shiz's people camped in Corihor's valley; Coriantumr camped in Shurr's valley near hill Comnor, gathered his armies on the hill, and sounded a trumpet to invite Shiz's armies to battle.
